title: The Parish of Ashcombe
premise: Ivo Galloway, an insurance investigator with a flawless photographic memory, receives two letters about the 1994 Ashcombe church fire that killed the parish's beloved vicar: one confessing to arson, the other promising 'more' if Ivo keeps digging. Drawn to the decaying Devon village, Ivo discovers the fire was insurance fraud layered over a darker secret—the vicar was already dead before the flames, and the town's most powerful family, the Verneys, built their fortune on the payout. As Ivo's memory reconstructs the night from fragments, they realize their own late mother was the vicar's housekeeper and a witness whose silence was bought, making Ivo's presence the final loose end someone means to erase. In the climax at the flooded quarry, Ivo confronts the surviving conspirator—now the parish's respected churchwarden—and chooses to expose the truth over protecting the one person left who loved their mother, ending with the Verney fortune dissolved and Ivo finally letting go of a memory they can no longer trust.
about_author: Zephyrine Nakamura is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unsolved deaths in rural England before turning to fiction. They write from a converted vestry on the Cornish coast, where they claim the fog does half the plotting.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Ivo Galloway, in their cluttered London flat, receives twin letters about the 1994 Ashcombe fire—one a confession, one a threat. Ivo's POV establishes their photographic memory and emotional detachment. The beat: curiosity overriding a lifetime rule never to revisit closed cases.

chapters.title: The Case I Closed
chapters.summary: Ivo retrieves their memory of the original insurance file, reconstructing the fire report in perfect detail—and noticing for the first time the discrepancy in the vicar's remains. Ivo's POV. The beat: the first crack in their faith in their own infallibility.

chapters.title: Arrival at Ashcombe
chapters.summary: Ivo arrives in the rain-soaked village, posing as an archivist. Through their eyes, Ashcombe is a place performing normalcy. They meet innkeeper Maren, who watches too carefully. The beat: the unsettling sense of being expected.

chapters.title: The Verney Pew
chapters.summary: At Sunday service, Ivo observes churchwarden Edmund Verney, patriarch of the family that received the fire payout. Edmund's charm is impeccable; his greeting to Ivo is a half-second too warm. Ivo's POV. The beat: recognition of a man who knows why they've come.

chapters.title: Housekeeper's Daughter
chapters.summary: Maren reveals Ivo's mother, Sable, was the vicar's housekeeper who left Ashcombe weeks after the fire and never spoke of it. Ivo's POV, shaken. The beat: the case turns personal—this village remembers their mother.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Ivo interviews the fire's surviving witnesses: the organist, the retired constable, the Verney son Tobias. Each alibi is airtight—too airtight, rehearsed across decades. Ivo's POV. The beat: mounting dread that the conspiracy is the whole village.

chapters.title: What Sable Saw
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Ivo finds their mother's statement from 1994, then a second, contradictory draft withdrawn before filing. Ivo's POV, grief and fury braided together. The beat: their mother's silence was purchased—and Ivo was raised on the proceeds of it.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Sender
chapters.summary: Ivo traces the threatening letter's paper to the village shop and narrows the sender to three people. That night, their rental cottage is searched. Ivo's POV. The beat: from hunter to hunted.

chapters.title: Tobias Verney's Confession of Sorts
chapters.summary: Tobias, the dissolute heir, drunkenly admits he signed the insurance claim he never read, and that his father 'handled the vicar.' Ivo's POV, wary. The beat: a confession that explains everything and proves nothing.

chapters.title: The Organist's Silence
chapters.summary: The organist, dying and unafraid, tells Ivo the vicar was dead before the fire—she saw the body in the vestry—and that Sable saw it too. Ivo's POV. The beat: the truth confirmed, and the terrible knowledge that their mother knew.

chapters.title: A Memory That Lies
chapters.summary: Ivo re-examines their own childhood memory of Ashcombe and finds a gap—a day their perfect recall cannot retrieve. Ivo's POV, existential vertigo. The beat: the investigator's one infallible tool is compromised.

chapters.title: Maren's Room
chapters.summary: Ivo discovers Maren's hidden room: newspaper clippings, the original confession letter's draft, evidence Maren has been investigating for years. Confrontation. Maren's POV shift. The beat: ally or architect? Maren sent the first letter to finally force the truth out.

chapters.title: The Constable's Ledger
chapters.summary: The retired constable, terrified, gives Ivo his old pocket ledger: the coroner was paid to record death by misadventure, ordered by Edmund Verney. Ivo's POV. The beat: the machinery of corruption laid bare, and a deadline—the constable is found dead the next morning.

chapters.title: Funeral for a Witness
chapters.summary: At the constable's funeral, the village closes ranks around Edmund. Ivo reads the congregation like a crime scene: who grieves, who performs. Ivo's POV. The beat: isolation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Vicar's Secret
chapters.summary: Ivo uncovers why the vicar died: he'd discovered the Verneys were embezzling parish restoration funds and threatened to expose them; the fire was to destroy his evidence and stage his death as accidental. Ivo's POV. The beat: motive complete, proof absent.

chapters.title: Sable's Letter
chapters.summary: Among Maren's papers is an unposted letter Sable wrote before fleeing, naming what she saw and begging forgiveness. Ivo reads their mother's voice across thirty years. Ivo's POV, devastated. The beat: understanding the woman who chose survival over truth.

chapters.title: The Quarry at Dusk
chapters.summary: Ivo stages a trap, letting Edmund believe they've found the vicar's remains. He lures them to the flooded quarry where the body was weighted. Edmund's POV shift reveals his self-justifications—everything done for family, parish, order. The beat: the predator showing his face.

chapters.title: Water Rising
chapters.summary: Edmund tries to drown Ivo in the quarry; Tobias, arriving to stop his father, is struck down. Ivo's photographic memory becomes weapon and burden—reciting Edmund's own recorded words back at him as Maren and the constable's grandson intervene. Ivo's POV. The beat: climax—truth as the only weapon left.

chapters.title: The Arrest
chapters.summary: Edmund is taken; the quarry is dredged and the vicar's remains found where Ivo's reconstructed memory placed them. Ivo's POV, hollow with exhaustion. The beat: victory that costs—Tobias in hospital, Maren complicit in obstruction, the village's soul exposed.

chapters.title: What the Parish Owes
chapters.summary: The Verney fortune is clawed back; the parish, bankrupted by scandal, must sell. Villagers who stayed silent for thirty years must reckon with what loyalty bought them. Ivo's POV observing the reckoning. The beat: justice without absolution.

chapters.title: Forgiving Sable
chapters.summary: Ivo visits their mother's grave and, for the first time, deliberately chooses to let a memory soften rather than hold it perfect—grieving the mother, not the witness. Ivo's POV. The beat: the emotional resolution of the loyalty-vs-truth theme.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: Weeks later, a third letter arrives: another confession, another village, another fire. Ivo reads it twice, then packs a bag. Ivo's POV. The beat: the investigator who can no longer stay invisible—and no longer wants to.
